items.q: During a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, which anatomical landmark combination fulfills the Strasberg Critical View of Safety before clipping or dividing any tubular structures?
o: Identification of the junction between cystic duct and common bile duct
Dissection of the hepatoduodenal ligament exposing the common hepatic artery
Clearing fat from hepatocystic triangle, mobilizing lower third of gallbladder off cystic plate, and visualizing exactly two structures entering the gallbladder
Visualizing the cystic lymph node of Lund and infundibular traction alone
items.exp: The Strasberg Critical View of Safety mandates: (1) clearing the hepatocystic triangle of all fat and fibrous tissue, (2) mobilizing the lower third of the gallbladder off the cystic plate (liver bed), and (3) confirming that exactly two structures (cystic duct and cystic artery) enter the gallbladder. Dissecting the common bile duct is dangerous and explicitly avoided.
r: Incorrect. Exposing the junction with the common bile duct increases the risk of duct injury.
Incorrect. Routine dissection of the hepatoduodenal ligament is dangerous and unnecessary.
Correct. The Critical View requires clearing the hepatocystic triangle, freeing the lower gallbladder from cystic plate, and confirming only two structures enter the organ.
Incorrect. Traction on the infundibulum alone does not ensure safety against misidentification.
items.kp: Critical View of Safety requires clearing the hepatocystic triangle, detaching lower 1/3 from cystic plate, and seeing only 2 structures.
